_comment: Hand-maintained page content. Read src/data/README.md before editing: it says who reads the page, what each field is for, and how to check the result. `npm test` validates the structure.
name: Cale McCammon
intro:
These are my public projects. The recent ones are a Kotlin-to-Lua compiler, a Go alerting service over Postgres, batch and streaming data pipelines, a benchmark for text-to-SQL models, and mobile apps in Flutter and React Native. The older repositories, from 2018 on, are Android and Java.

Six are described below. The rest are in the repository list at the bottom of the page.

featured.summary: A compiler from Kotlin to plain, readable Lua. It targets Lua 5.1 to 5.4 and LuaJIT, and runs as a command-line tool or a Gradle plugin.
points: Parsing and type checking go through the Kotlin Analysis API. Kotlin that k2l cannot translate is a compile error.
The output needs no third-party Lua code. The compiler copies in only the parts of its own Lua runtime that a program uses.
More than 250 golden test programs are compiled and run on all five Lua interpreters in CI.

featured.summary: Delay alerts for Finnish cargo rail. A Go service over Postgres polls an open rail API on a schedule and notifies once per late train per day, however many polls see the delay.
points: Duplicate suppression is a UNIQUE constraint with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so two overlapping poll runs cannot both send the same alert.
Sign-in is GitHub OAuth, and the database stores only a SHA-256 hash of each session token.
Webhook URLs come from users, so the service guards against SSRF: it rejects private addresses, re-checks the IP after DNS resolution, and does not follow redirects.

featured.summary: A Flutter app for Android and the web that shows live Finnish freight traffic: cargo trains from a GraphQL API, vessels and port calls from a REST API.
points: The domain logic is a separate pure-Dart package with no Flutter imports. Both APIs sit behind one repository class, so the UI never handles GraphQL or HTTP types.
The rail and marine feeds share no identifier. The app joins them by pairing each train's final station with the nearest seaport that has port calls.
118 tests run with every external call mocked, and CI builds and deploys the web version.

featured.summary: A benchmark for text-to-SQL models. It runs each generated query against a fixed DuckDB warehouse and compares the rows with the reference query's rows, so differently written but correct SQL still passes.
points: The comparison rules are documented and tested: row order counts only when the reference query has a top-level ORDER BY, rows compare as a multiset, and floats compare within a tolerance.
Generated SQL is treated as untrusted input. Only a single read statement is allowed, and it runs in an in-memory database with file access off and a 15-second timeout.
In the committed run, llama3.2 answered 22 of 72 questions correctly. With table names but no column names in the prompt it answered 1 of 24, and 56% of all failures were unknown-column errors.

featured.summary: An ELT pipeline for stock prices and macroeconomic indicators. It loads Yahoo Finance and FRED data into DuckDB or BigQuery, models it with dbt, schedules it with Dagster, and publishes an Evidence dashboard.
points: The dbt project has staging, intermediate and mart layers ending in a star schema, with custom SQL tests and source freshness checks.
The same pipeline runs on DuckDB locally and on BigQuery in the cloud. One environment variable selects the target.
The dashboard carries a market briefing written by Gemini. Every figure in it is checked against the source data first, and a briefing that fails the check is retried once and then withheld.

featured.summary: A Kafka Streams application in Kotlin that aggregates the live stream of Wikipedia edits and serves the results over a REST API.
points: It keeps three aggregations: edits per wiki in one-minute tumbling windows, the most-edited pages in five-minute hopping windows, and a running ratio of bot to human edits.
The API reads the application's own RocksDB state stores through interactive queries, so there is no separate database.
The topologies are unit-tested with TopologyTestDriver, which needs no running broker.
